scope: Source-only HTTP adapter review; no server/browser/Cargo/GPU/renderer execution.

findings.title: Record the actual termination reason in the cleanup receipt
findings.detail: The cleanup receipt chooses stdin quit for every self.stopping exit, but connection-budget exhaustion (304-309), request-budget exhaustion (186-188), and control-input overflow (277-280) also set that flag. An exception in the try block instead reports overall watchdog even if no deadline expired. This loses the final invalid/unavailable reason for an incomplete browser trial.
findings.source_reproducer: Without sending quit, accept a 129th connection or provide more than 4096 buffered stdin bytes. The explicit branches set stopping and finally labels the exit stdin quit. No runtime replay performed.
findings.recommendation: Keep an explicit stop_reason, record exception/invalid or unavailable outcomes truthfully, and include the terminal reason in status/cleanup rather than deriving it from the stopping boolean.

source_checks: Fixture must be 3827840 bytes with exact f13e0189ae9a1bed17d7cf3e367e495d81ffd31b9a050b76dc1cf2e5bdff6eb6 digest.
Twelve Work variants deep-copy the canonical Work and change only profile.asset_path. Asset routes return the unmodified fixture.
Single selector loop, no response threads; active connection cap 20, total accepted/request budget 128, bounded headers/input/chunks/static file size, loopback-only 9204.
First four held GETs do not block admission observation: an extra GET while four remain held and none released emits product_bound_claim_allowed=false and is served rather than held.

Default body hold 90 seconds and overall loop deadline 120 seconds; holds and sockets close in finally; accepted must equal closed. These are loop-driven deadlines, not proof against a process blocked writing its log/stdout.
Client closures, automatic hold releases, budget rejections and all request counts are observable in the raw event log.
proof_preconditions: The adapter alone cannot establish twelve GUI Opens in one running Web App or count CharacterAsset.retiring; do not infer these from twelve Work GETs.

Root must retain one-document-instance GUI evidence, final frozen Web artifact identity, all twelve requested paths, visible wait/error, and latest-document recovery. Twelve navigations are invalid for this test.

During the full-capacity observation window require asset GETs exactly once for four distinct paths, four simultaneously held bodies, and no prior release/connection closure/watchdog/budget rejection. A fifth asset GET before a real release invalidates the bound claim; held_bodies alone is capped by the adapter and cannot prove the product cap.

Releases and later GETs need sequence checking: after one explicit release only latest pending stall-12 may start. Automatic release or premature disconnection makes the intended hold trial unavailable/incomplete.
Current baseline/control receipts are direct HTTP adapter-only evidence. They do not establish browser behavior or final-candidate behavior.
receipt_checks: Frozen-baseline control raw log has 12 distinct Work GETs, first four held, explicit release of 01, GET 12, five 3827840-byte transfers, then accepted=closed=17 with zero active/held connections.
Watchdog raw log has hold release at 0.2096 seconds and overall cleanup at 1.0259 seconds, accepted=closed=1; this tests short configured watchdogs, not actual 90/120 second dwell.
Neither supplied control receipt exercises unexpected fifth fetch before release, connection budget, oversized stdin, or exceptional-exit labeling.
